title: The three-small-triangles conjecture for five points
source: Matthew Kahle, “Points in a triangle forcing small triangles”, arXiv:0811.2449 (2008). (https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.2449), Conjecture 3.1

lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-362667-317945-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-317945.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: For any triangle of area 1 in the plane and any five points of the closed triangle (not necessarily distinct), at least three of the ten unordered triples of the points span a triangle of area at most 1/4, where degenerate triples count with area 0. This is Kahle's three-small-triangles conjecture; three cannot be replaced by four. The proof is a case analysis on the midpoint subdivision with a determinant identity; the reduction from an arbitrary triangle to a standard one is proved in Lean.
significance.caveat: Degenerate triples are counted as small, the convention forced by the source's use of Soifer's one-triangle theorem. Soifer's book chapter on the problem (Springer) was not read; it is understood to reprint the 2008 material. Bounded literature search only.

root_basis: Root extracted the six modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms exactly the allowed three, no forbidden tokens), and screened the Principia archive (300 ids), the omega registry and GitHub by id. An independent Opus referee checked that the Lean statement is literal and cannot hold vacuously, verified the result with its own scripts from the source definitions, read the paper line by line and supplied the revised paper used here.
